OPERATING CASH FLOW BEFORE WORKING CAPITAL CHANGES, FREE CASH FLOW AND FREE CASH FLOW MARGIN Operating cash flow before working capital changes, which is a non-GAAP financial measure, represents net cash provided by operating activities as determined under GAAP without regard to changes in operating assets and liabilities. The Company believes operating cash flow before working capital changes is a useful measure of the Company’s ability to generate cash to fund acquisition activities, service debt or pay dividends. The Company also uses this measure because changes in operating assets and liabilities relate to the timing of cash receipts and disbursements that the Company may not control and may not relate to the period in which the operating activities occurred. The Company defines Free Cash Flow, which is a non-GAAP financial measure, as operating cash flow before working capital changes in excess of capital expenditures. The Company defines Free Cash Flow margin as Free Cash Flow divided by total operating income. The Company believes that Free Cash Flow and Free Cash Flow margin are useful to investors as they provide a measure to compare cash flow from operating activities across periods on a consistent basis. These measures should not be considered as alternatives to, or more meaningful than, net cash provided by operating activities as an indicator of liquidity. The Company's computations of Free Cash Flow and Free Cash Flow margin may not be comparable to other similarly titled measures of other companies. THIRD QUARTER 2026 CASH DIVIDEND & CAPITAL RETURN PROGRAM Viper announced today that the Company’s Board of Directors (the “Board”) declared a base cash dividend of $0.50 per Class A common share for the third quarter of 2026, payable on November 19, 2026 to Class A common stockholders of record at the close of business on November 12, 2026. During the third quarter of 2026, Viper repurchased approximately 2.1 million shares of the Company’s Class A common stock for an aggregate purchase price of approximately $90 million, excluding excise tax (average price of $43.01 per share). In total, since the initiation of Viper’s common stock repurchase program on November 9, 2020 through October 30, 2026, the Company has repurchased approximately 26.1 million shares of common stock (including both Class A shares and Class B shares paired with OpCo Units) for an aggregate purchase price of approximately $844 million, excluding excise tax (average price of $32.30 per share) and has approximately $906 million remaining on its share buyback authorization. Future cash dividends and stock repurchases are at the discretion of the Board and are subject to a number of factors discussed in Viper’s reports filed with the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission (“SEC”). OPERATIONS UPDATE During the third quarter of 2026, Viper estimates that 689 gross (19.0 net 100% royalty interest) horizontal wells, normalized to lateral length of 10,000 feet, with an average royalty interest of 2.8% were turned to production on its acreage position. Of these 689 gross wells, Diamondback is the operator of 123 gross wells, with an average royalty interest of 9.4%, and the remaining 566 gross wells, with an average royalty interest of 1.3%, are operated by third parties. As of September 30, 2026, Viper’s footprint of mineral and royalty interests was approximately 98,098 net royalty acres.
